title: A terminal opened with a command (cmd, an agent) shows its first output about 1.2 s after a bare start would
finding: Not herdr-core: the app runs every argv inside the person's interactive PowerShell (agent_argv: powershell.exe -NoExit -Command "& 'cmd.exe'"), so PowerShell's own start (~0.55 s) plus their profile (~0.6 s) comes before the program; the harness's own core connection sending that same argv is just as slow, and no ESC[6n or other query appears in either byte stream.

metrics.name: cmd prompt sent by core: app terminal.open (before) vs harness client sending the app's wrapped argv, no app (after)
what-if, harness client: app's wrapper (before) vs the same wrapper with -NoProfile (after)
what-if, harness client: app's wrapper (before) vs bare cmd.exe argv, no wrapper (after)

notes: No app code changed, so there is no after run. The baseline's 'app adds +1171 ms' compared different commands: open.tab.cmd runs tab.new argv [cmd.exe], which the app wraps in PowerShell, while open.core_alone.cmd runs bare cmd.exe. Env (COLORTERM, TERM_PROGRAM), on:null and labels each made no difference (79-122 ms). In the raw stream both paths send the same ConPTY setup, \e[1t and \e[?1004h\e[?9001h within 70-150 ms; the wrapped path then waits until \e[?7l\e[?7h at 1270-1540 ms, while PowerShell starts and runs cmd. The wrapper is documented ('Agents run in your interactive shell, which stays open after the agent exits', defaults/AGENTS.md:688) and Unix has the same shape (sh -ic 'prog; exec sh -i'), so any change needs the maintainer: (a) -NoProfile on the wrapper saves ~0.6 s here but loses profile PATH/aliases for the program and for the shell that stays; (b) start a program that is itself a shell (cmd, powershell, pwsh) bare, saving ~1.1 s, but exiting it would close the pane instead of leaving PowerShell; (c) the core's pre-started spare shell (bottleneck #1) would hide it, but that needs herdr-core. The default-shell path (no argv) is not wrapped and has no stall. scripts/perf/open_delay.py now includes the 'own client, app's argv' case.

title: The window no longer freezes for 50-100 ms each time a tab, split or space opens; it keeps drawing while the terminal starts
finding: Every new terminal made the UI thread wait in Core::call_timeout (recv_timeout) for the core's synchronous terminal.run reply while the core started the process (ui:spawn_terminal equalled rpc:terminal.run, 45-56 ms median); no app-side file I/O or spawn was involved.

metrics.name: main-thread time per tab.new (cmd:tab.new + ui:place_terminal), focused, window kept drawing by hover
longest main-thread task while a tab opens (focused)
longest gap between drawn frames while a tab opens (focused)
frames drawn while a tab opens (focused)

notes: terminal.run now runs on the background executor (start_open) and the pane is placed when it answers (finish_open, ui:place_terminal ~7.5 ms, mostly ui:sync). Order kept: while one starts, every command (keys, clicks, mods, zaki do) waits in a FIFO and runs after it is placed, so a double press makes two tabs in order and a rename sent 3 ms after tab.new renames the new tab, as before; zaki do replies arrive when the pane is placed, same shape. reconcile skips adoption while one starts (the core's created event can beat the reply). Quit/WM_CLOSE mid-open: drain_documents waits for it, places it and saves it (checked: the tab and terminal survive a relaunch, same as before). Window gone without placing: the terminal is killed. Deliberate difference: if a split's target pane (or a tab's space) closes during the ~50 ms, the command now fails ('no pane ...: it closed while its terminal started') and its terminal is killed; before, the close could not be processed until the split landed, so the split replaced the closed pane. Keystrokes (follow-up commit after 0471fbd): 0471fbd sent keys typed within ~50 ms of the shortcut to the old pane. Now, while a terminal the person asked for starts and a terminal has the keyboard, the root capture_key_down holds each keystroke in the same FIFO as commands (paste is a command, so it waits too) and replays it with window.dispatch_keystroke once the pane is placed: bindings and text go to the pane focused then, the previous one if the start failed. The pointer, hover and non-terminal focus are never held. A new pane also keeps input typed before its first attach (up to 64 KiB) and sends it on attach: before fix 2 such keys were dropped, since the new pane had no channel yet. open_behaviour.py keys, F9 bound to tab.new then 'echo zqN' + Enter posted at once or 40 ms later: before fix 2, 0 of 10 bytes reached any pane (6/6 reps); 0471fbd, the old pane; now 10/10 bytes to the new pane's channel and the text in its shell (6/6), and to the old pane when the start fails on a missing folder (3/3). Back-to-back focused run under heavy load (582-1967% of a core busy): main-thread per open 86.0 -> 21.9 ms, longest frame gap 131 -> 49 ms, attached 141 -> 136 ms. The split-target-closed difference stays: neither defaults/AGENTS.md nor src/SKILL.md describes that race; the old outcome only came from the blocked UI thread not processing the close event. rpc:terminal.attach rose 1.4 -> 12-14 ms but runs off the main thread (terminal.rs:239); attach and first output times are unchanged, the core is simply still setting up when the attach comes in sooner. Full run 20261103-104948 had 2x the background load (626% vs 296% of a core busy at start); its 25-45% rises in untouched code (hover, mod loads) and +12% in shell start (bare PowerShell +12%, core alone +10%) vanished in a back-to-back A/B (20261103-105608-ab-before-frames vs 20261103-110115-ab-after-frames, --only frames,open). Focused measurements: scratchpad open_frames.py (15 opens under posted hover) and open_behaviour.py (double, order, closing, quit), not in the repo. Platform-neutral change: the blocking call is the same on every OS. cargo test --release: 214 pass; two tests already fail on HEAD (8b0286f) on Windows, not from this work: window::tests::fitted_popups_use_their_rendered_size_at_the_window_edge and mods::render_tests::packed_path_points_keep_their_order_around_other_commands; a_0_1_x_layout_is_kept_aside_quietly_not_rescued is flaky only in parallel.

title: Zaki opens about 0.4 s sooner (first frame at 0.9 s instead of 1.3 s), and its very first start about 1.3 s sooner
finding: Every start re-read and hashed all ~499 shipped mod files (plus a stat per entry), deleted and rewrote the 29 frame files, and on an empty home wrote 139 icons atomically inside open_window, all one after the other on the main thread before the platform even started.

cold.fresh.start:installs_wait_ms (main thread): one mod at a time vs all mods at once, back-to-back

notes: Three parts. (1) Skip work: installed-stamps.json (new, beside installed.json, listed in defaults/AGENTS.md) keeps, per default mod and for frame/, each file's size and modified time (ns) from the folder listing taken BEFORE the files were last read and found as shipped, plus the fingerprint of what they were checked against. A start lists the folders (no file opened; DirEntry metadata) and skips a mod only if installed.json says it is the shipped version AND every file looks exactly as stamped; anything else (an edit, an added or deleted file, a link, a new release, a missing or corrupt stamp file) takes the old read-and-hash path unchanged. Stamps are kept only for files modified at least 2 s before the check, so a file written by a start is read once more on the next start before it is trusted, and an edit can't share a stamped time. frame/ is no longer deleted and rewritten each start: left alone while it is as shipped (same check), else rewritten whole as before, so edits still don't stick. Hidden files and gpui-shell's gpui-kit.d.ts/jsconfig.json are ignored exactly as as_shipped ignores them. Tests: an edit of the same size given an OLD modified time while the app was closed, an added file and a deleted file are all still caught (moved to -edited, restored); a release that changes the defaults replaces stamped mods, keeps edits as clones, leaves an unchanged mod on its stamp; fresh writes are never stamped; frame edits/additions/new release rewrite it. Remaining undetectable case: a tool that writes a file and then sets its size and modified time back to the exact stamped values to the nanosecond (100 ns on NTFS). (2) Overlap: write_workspace and the themes/icons install (moved out of AppWindow::new, 635 ms on an empty home) run on two threads started right after update::apply_on_startup, beside core_find, core_connect and the platform start, and are joined at the top of the platform's run callback, before fonts, mods init, the control socket and the window, so the first frame shows the same files. They take the home path from the main thread and read no environment (core_bin::use_core sets PATH meanwhile; its SAFETY note updated). On the setup screen path the themes/icons are now written at start instead of when the main window opens (same files, earlier). (3) First run: the default mods' and frame's files are written by 4 threads (write_files), after every mod's decisions and renames; fresh write_workspace 782-808 -> 374-377 ms, fresh first paint 1494 (one writer) -> 1260-1287 ms. Follow-up commit: mods are written one at a time again (each mod's old folder moved aside, then its own files written by up to 4 writers when it has 16 or more), so a failed write leaves every later mod exactly as before and installed.json unsaved, as the old code did (test a_failed_write_leaves_the_other_mods_as_they_were: injected NUL file name in b of a,b,c; a updated, c untouched, record unchanged; the next start keeps a and b as -edited clones and installs all three, as before). Platform-neutral change (the same work on every OS; nothing gated). Measurement: the machine was under heavy outside load throughout (500-2100% of a core busy in other processes; core alone throughput 270 -> 18 MB/s and bare PowerShell +77% between the two full runs, no app involved), so the headline numbers are the back-to-back cold-only A/B (ab-cold-head-1, fixB-1, fixA-1, head-2, fixB-2, prebuilt binaries via --no-build --bin); the full after run (20261103-122728) is the fix without the parallel writes. Every non-cold metric the full compare flagged moved with the load (no-app readings moved the same way) in code this change doesn't touch. Unconfirmed, one run: frames.settings ui:mod_load 113 -> 37 ms (Settings is a frame mod; it is no longer rewritten each start). Remaining before first paint on a warm start: platform start ~330 ms, open_window ~300 ms (mod loads ~100), core_find ~80 ms (hc --version even when settings name the core) and core_connect ~75 ms still serial; caching the core's version is the next step. Tests: cargo test --release 217 pass; the two failures already on HEAD remain (fitted_popups..., packed_path_points...), and notices failed since 46935c8 (ours: the harness added 5 windows-sys features to Cargo.toml, so its Input-SHA256 no longer matched). Regenerating needs cargo-about 0.9.3, not installed, so instead the follow-up commit puts Cargo.toml back exactly as before 46935c8 and the profiler (src/bench/sampler.rs) declares its own kernel32 calls and types (CONTEXT x64 with compile-time size/offset checks, THREADENTRY32, MODULEINFO), as it already did for NtQueryInformationThread and QueryThreadCycleTime; wndproc.rs uses std::process::id(). The notices test itself is unchanged; a new sampler test samples a busy thread and checks it is listed, named and unwound through this program. The 'flaky in parallel' a_0_1_x_layout test was the global sync-notes list; the six tests that make or check notes now take turns (notes_turn), 3/3 clean runs. .gitignore: __pycache__/. Cost of writing one mod at a time (A/B ab-cold-fixC-1/2 vs ab-cold-fixB-3/4, under more load than the first A/B): write_workspace on its thread 384-413 -> 608-615 ms on an empty home, but the window waits 4-65 ms vs 34 ms and first paint 1436-1450 -> 1527-1529 ms (+6%, within the 126-257 ms spread); the empty-home headline above (measured with all mods at once) stands within noise. Warm starts are unaffected (write_workspace 40-49 ms either way).

title: Opening Settings no longer freezes the window for most of a second, and gets much less slow each time it's opened
finding: While a newly loaded mod copy warms up, the QuickJS JIT's maintenance rebuilds a deep copy of its whole feedback table about 190 times per Settings open on the UI thread (80% of main-thread samples), and the table grows with every open because gpui-shell loads each copy as a new module generation that QuickJS never frees.

metrics.name: frames.settings.frame_main_thread_ms
metrics.spread: harness single run each; median rose because many more open frames fit the stretch

metrics.name: settings later open: command to drawn (A/B)
settings first open after start: command to drawn (A/B)
settings 10th open: command to drawn / worst frame (A/B, median of 4 rounds)
metrics.spread: per-open medians; second figure is the worst frame

notes: Kept as a vendored-engine HERDR: patch (approved by the user) in vendor/quickjs-jit-runtime/src/runtime/feedback.rs, listed in its Cargo.toml header; offer it upstream to longbridge/quickjs-jit. Each feedback lattice cell keeps the shared copy a snapshot holds (Entry::shared; whole call and call-signature entries in `frozen`), made again only when that cell changes, so FeedbackTable::snapshot copies pointers instead of allocating every list. Exact: a snapshot equals one built from scratch (new test snapshot_cache_tests::kept_copies_follow_every_change, every mutator incl. forget_function and megamorphic widening). Not fixed, for the maintainer: the module-generation leak. gpui-shell load_app (vendor/gpui-kit/crates/shell/src/engine/quickjs/mod.rs:2194) makes every load a new generation (main.js?v=N); QuickJS frees evaluated modules only in JS_FreeContext, so every overlay load (Settings, palette, help, menus, toasts) keeps its bytecode and its JIT feedback for the life of the app. Settings adds about 770 feedback entries per open (2,831 -> 9,744 over 8 opens); with the patch opens still slow a little each time (252 -> 403 ms drawn over 10 opens, against 329 -> 1077 ms on HEAD). Reusing an unchanged mod's modules would change mod semantics (module top level once per copy), so it needs the maintainer. Ruled out: caching the whole snapshot until the next change (no gain, one build per pass anyway); a Zaki-side Settings change (layouts()/themes() once per render, previews with settings.json: worst frame 448 -> 737 ms, reverted). Bottleneck #8 plays no part (ui:refresh_mods 0.02 ms per open). The palette, also a frame mod, is small: about 200 ms drawn and 20 ms worst frame either way. Other harness metrics within noise. The harness run with the patch is 20261103-163607-quickjs-patch-settings.json (label corrected from fix-settings-stall). Tests: cargo test --release --locked -j 4: 220 pass, 2 fail as on HEAD (fitted_popups..., packed_path_points...); the crate's 64 lib tests pass (run via a temporary [workspace] table and lockfile copy, both removed).

title: Moving the pointer over the window was measured at 60 redraws a second and 40-50% of a core; with a real pointer it redraws only when the row or tab under it changes (about 8-18 a second when sweeping, none inside one row), about 10-15% of a core
finding: Not the app: the harness posts its pointer moves while the real cursor is elsewhere, so every TrackMouseEvent(TME_LEAVE) that gpui's Windows backend asks for on a move (gpui-pre-windows events.rs:1425) gets an immediate WM_MOUSELEAVE, the window flips hovered/not on every move and gpui refreshes the whole window for each flip (gpui-pre window.rs:1979); a real pointer is over the window when it moves and never flips.

notes: A measurement fix, not an app change: what people see and do is unchanged (no vendor change). With HERDR_APP_BENCH_POSTED_POINTER, which scripts/perf/instance.py now sets for every test instance, the bench window-procedure wrapper (only attached with HERDR_APP_BENCH_EVENTS, Windows only) drops WM_MOUSELEAVE, so the test window behaves as under a real pointer; new test only_a_posted_pointer_loses_its_leave. How it was found: a temporary probe in gpui-pre (saved as scratchpad hover-probe.patch, reverted) counted every App::notify / Window::refresh / refresh_windows / request_animation_frame by #[track_caller] caller, split by whether a mouse move was being dispatched. Moving 1 px inside one sidebar row (nothing under the pointer changes) drew ~42-59 fps, all from window.rs:1979 (on_hover_status_change), none inside the move dispatch; the sidebar and tab sweeps added only div.rs:2866 notifies (gpui's hover style, edge-triggered: one per row/tab crossed, ~10/s and ~25/s). With leave ignored, frames equal those transitions and the still case draws nothing. HEAD's numbers depend on where the person's cursor is: in reps where it happened to be over the test window the flips stopped (HEAD tab/still fps iqr 15.6 / 59.4), and the baseline ran with it elsewhere. No user-visible fix was needed for 'redraw only when something changes': gpui's div hover styles, on_hover and tooltips all notify only on a transition, mods notify only on drags (spaces, tabs, tabs-column), the app's root and terminal move handlers only on drags or Ctrl-links, and gpui-shell adds no notify of its own. What remains for a real pointer, for later: (1) each transition is a whole-window draw of ~3.5-5 ms main thread: the hovered mod view is notified, gpui marks every ancestor dirty, so AppWindow::render rebuilds the whole layout tree (terminals and mod views are cached: ShellRoot caches its mod, window.rs:4122; terminals via cached(), window.rs:4431); cutting that needs the layout split into cached views, a bigger change in src/window.rs. (2) Moves alone cost ~5% of a core at 125 moves/s with nothing drawn (still: 9-10% vs ~5% idle): hit-testing plus JS on_mouse_move calls the spaces (main.js:290) and tabs (main.js:433) mods register on every row/bar although they only act during a drag; registering them only while pressed would remove the JS calls; a 1000 Hz mouse makes this 8x. (3) Real-pointer case that still flips: a drag with the pointer outside the window (capture) gets a leave per move, but gpui redraws every move of a drag anyway. Other metrics: the full runs flagged rises in palette/settings/help mod loads (+35-130%), scrollback paint_grid, cold (+6-9%) and split open (+8%) under rising outside load (747 -> 944% of a core busy); none touches this code, and the back-to-back frames-only A/B (20261103-191600-ab-frames-head5 vs 20261103-191815-ab-frames-fix5) shows them flat or lower (scrollback 6.28 -> 5.15 ms per frame, 57.4 -> 55.7 fps; palette mod_load 16.3 -> 16.3 ms). tab_switch now draws fewer frames (4.35 -> 3.19 fps) because the flip after the pointer is parked no longer adds frames. The before run used HEAD 5486787 built here (scratchpad bins/zaki-head5.exe) and the after run the fix (bins/zaki-fix5.exe), both with --no-build from the same working tree; the HEAD binary ignores the new variable, so 'before' is the old measurement. Focused A/B: scratchpad hover.py (sidebar, tab bar and 1 px still stretches, 5 reps of 5 s after a warm-up, isolated instance). Another Claude session (05cdc673) ran a full-core cargo build in the main repo when this started, so this worker waited for it before building. Tests: cargo test --release --locked -j 4: 221 pass, 2 fail as on HEAD (fitted_popups..., packed_path_points...).

title: An agent whose title changes costs about 40% less mod script time and about 2 points less CPU: only the panels that show what changed redraw
finding: Every change the window publishes (an agent's title, a terminal listing, focus) re-ran the script of every mod copy on screen, about 10 ms per event (8.8-11.6) and 2 events per title change (the pane title, then the core's terminal listing), though most copies never read the part that changed; the terminal listing alone is read by only 4 of the 9 shown copies.

notes: Each copy's herdr module (built per copy) records which live parts (spaces, machines, agents, panes, terminals, focused, layout, window, placement) the copy has ever read; publish turns what changed into a part mask and refreshes only copies that read one of those parts. A part once read stays read, so a copy that reads agents() in a timer or init still sees every change to it. Theme, settings, shared, update status and Request::Refresh still refresh every copy, and refresh is still marked dirty + notify, so GPUI still coalesces to one build per frame and each copy reads the newest snapshot. Mod API, what mods are told and defaults/AGENTS.md are unchanged. Same on every platform (no OS gate): the fan-out is platform-independent. Idle with one terminal has no refreshes; its app CPU (about 3.8% vs 4.1% over 9 reps each) is noise, with the window thread equal or lower. frames.settings dropped_frames 12 -> 93 is the known bimodal settings warm-up (9-184 on unchanged code across earlier runs); fps 3.3 -> 6.8, p95 main 739 -> 278. Tests: 222 pass incl. the new lifecycle test; the 2 known Windows failures (fitted_popups..., packed_path_points...) as before. Busy terminals in a hidden tab still refresh their readers; what changes there was not traced. Does not touch the spaces/tabs on_mouse_move path.
